newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine hog raisers plan to buy 150,000 T corn.
newsitem.headline: Philippine hog raisers plan to buy 150,000 T corn.

text.p: Philippine hog raisers plan to buy 150,000 tonnes of corn in the fourth quarter, traders and industry executives said on Friday.
"We have asked the (state-owned) National Food Authority (NFA) to import for us," said an industry executive.
On Tuesday, feed millers had said they have asked the NFA to import for them another 150,000 tonnes in anticipation of the lean months in the first quarter of 1997.
The private sector usually asks the NFA to import grains for them in order to avail of lower tariffs.
The Philippines has imported 250,000 tonnes of corn from the United States and Argentina since the start of the year to meet increasing demand of the commodity for animal feed.
Traders blamed a drop in the country's corn output to the rise in the importation of the grain.

"In crop year 1990-1991 ending July, corn output reached 4.8 million tonnes. Last year, production dropped to 4.2 million," an industry executive said, adding that shortage of corn has spawned an increase in the importation of soymeal as substitute.
Local consumption of imported soymeal for animal feed rose to 950,000 tonnes last year from 450,000 tonnes in 1990, the executive added.
Traders said the NFA's high support price on local corn may entice farmers to increase production in the short term.
"But when it (NFA) runs out of money to buy local produce, it will be more difficult for everybody," said the executive.
Traders said U.S. corn is currently trading at $150 to $160 per tonne for nearby months while the NFA is buying corn at $250 per tonne in the southern Mindanao island.

The executive said the high price of corn in the local market would increase the cost of hog raisers and make the local industry less competitive in a free market for meat products. --Manila newsroom (632) 841-89-36, fax 817-62-67
